synopsis: The corpus distinguishes a quick prototype or pre-study from a safety-credible capability: VaViM’s six months in 2022 produced a pre-study, not an accepted virtual-validation capability, and no in-house open-source time-to-first-useful-result benchmark was found [f1207, f1551, f1552, f8741, f8742]. The recommended trust-earning pilot is a deliberately difficult, end-to-end thin slice covering one safety function and one or two machine variants, with physical or bench comparators, blind predictions, pre-registered metrics and explicit go, restricted-go, pivot and stop criteria—not a polished nominal-cycle demonstration [f9914, f9918, f9919, f9921]. The example pilot runs in months 3–5, uses 3–5 scenario classes including an edge case, and pre-specifies 10–30 physical test points; the evidence package is due by March 2027, followed by a proposed March–April 2027 credibility gate requiring acceptable blind-pilot results, assessor feedback and a P80 delivery date inside the deadline [f9915, f9916, f9917, f16270, f12306]. Pilot methodology supports feasibility testing and advance progression criteria, but its transfer from health and social research is an analogy rather than direct evidence for heavy-machine virtual testing [f9899, f9901, f9904, f9905]. Site pilots should follow controlled whole-machine confirmation near safety limits, use trained staff and explicit operational controls, and measure nuisance stops and missing operator-response data rather than assume passenger-car values [f884, f10988, f11138, f3617]. Planning should use pilots to inform bottom-up cost estimates and predefine useful fallback deliverables, including physical-test-backed claims, simulation-only scenario screening or engineering-learning results rather than safety credit [f10752, f11084, f12468].

relations.note: Both define a trust-earning pilot as a difficult thin slice with blind, pre-registered evaluation.
Glossary restates Chapter 12’s blind-prediction and pre-registration recommendation.
Both identify VaViM’s six months as a pre-study, not an accepted capability.
Glossary repeats the limitation of VaViM’s six-month duration.
Glossary repeats the difficult engineering pilot’s scope, comparators and pre-declared criteria.
Both recommend running the pilot in months three to five.
Both specify three to five scenario classes, including an edge case.
Both specify ten to thirty pre-selected physical test points.
Both describe the March–April 2027 G2 gate; f12306 also specifies assessor feedback.
Both recommend bottom-up estimates after pilots; the latter names cost-overrun risk.
Both distinguish feasibility from effectiveness and identify the borrowed research context.
Both require advance declaration of go, restricted-go, pivot and stop criteria.
Both characterize transferred pilot methodology as supporting analogy, not direct proof.
Chapter 4 broadens the glossary’s operator-behavior data recommendation to accidents and braking safety.
Specifies detection outcomes, rather than images alone, for the pre-registered sensor correlation metrics.
Potentially unacceptable false activations justify measuring nuisance stops per operating hour.
Controlled deployment pilots require prior whole-machine confirmation of virtual predictions near safety limits.
Unbenchmarked business-case assumptions motivate bottom-up estimates after pilots.
